newsitem.title: CHINA: Malaysian PM in China for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian PM in China for trade talks.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad arrived in Beijing on Saturday heading a 250-strong group of business leaders and government officials on an effort to boost trade and economic ties with China.
Malaysian officials said Mahathir was scheduled to hold talks with Chinese Premier Li Peng and to deliver a keynote address to a Malaysia-China Partnership meeting in Beijing.
At least 10 joint venture agreements would be signed between Malaysian and Chinese firms at the opening of the meeting, Malaysia's Bernam news agency said.
The four-day visit is Mahathir's fourth to China as Prime Minister.

Some of Malaysia's top corporate chiefs were expected to join their prime minister at the event, which was to be attended by about 700 participants, including 450 Chinese businessmen and government officials.
Bernam quoted Malaysian ambassador to China Amir Jaafar as saying Sino-Malaysian trade had grown rapidly since the signing of a bilateral trade agreement in 1988.
During the past five years, bilateral trade had increased from 3.2 billion ringgit ($1.2 billion) in 1990 to 8.4 billion in 1995, he said.
